subject: Digital Electronics
description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of digital systems, logic design, and circuit implementation. It emphasizes combinational and sequential logic, logic families, and digital components essential for computer systems.
objectives: Understand the basic concepts of number systems and Boolean algebra.
Design and simplify combinational and sequential logic circuits.
Familiarize with logic families and integrated circuits.
Analyze digital circuits using simulation tools.
Develop digital systems using standard combinational and sequential modules.
course_outcomes: Apply Boolean algebra to simplify and design digital circuits.
Design combinational logic circuits such as adders, multiplexers, and encoders.
Implement sequential logic circuits using flip-flops and registers.
Understand memory elements and programmable logic devices.
Analyze the performance of digital systems using timing diagrams and simulation tools.

modules.title: Number Systems and Boolean Algebra
topics: Binary, Octal, Decimal, and Hexadecimal Number Systems
Karnaugh Map Simplification up to 4 Variables

modules.title: Combinational Logic Circuits
topics: Implementation of Boolean Functions using MUX/DEMUX

modules.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
topics: Latches and Flip-Flops (SR, JK, D, T)
Design of Sequential Circuits from State Tables

modules.title: Logic Families and Digital Components
topics: Transistor-Transistor Logic (TTL), Emitter Coupled Logic (ECL), CMOS Logic
Characteristics of Logic Families – Fan-in, Fan-out, Noise Margin, Propagation Delay
Programmable Logic Devices – PLA, PAL, and FPGA Introduction

modules.title: Memory and Data Conversion
topics: Memory Organization and Classification – ROM, RAM, EPROM, EEPROM
Applications of Digital Circuits in Microprocessors and Embedded Systems

suggested_books: M. Morris Mano, Digital Logic and Computer Design, Pearson Education
R.P. Jain, Modern Digital Electronics, 4th Edition, McGraw-Hill Education
reference_books: Thomas L. Floyd, Digital Fundamentals, Pearson
Donald P. Leach and Albert Malvino, Digital Principles and Applications, McGraw-Hill
